newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch closing debt market report.
newsitem.headline: Dutch closing debt market report.

text.p: Brisk end-of-session trade pushed Dutch bonds higher on Friday after a day spent largely range-bound as market players digested a string of economic data from both sides of the Atlantic.
The cash market shrugged off disappointing German May jobless figures early in the session, as some leaked numbers were already discounted in the prices, traders said.
Bundesbank president Hans Tietmeyer's remarks that the economy was picking up speed were also seen as positive, one trader added.
Dealers said midsession trade had been thin ahead of a slew of U.S. labour market numbers, but a record low in unemployment in May had surprisingly little effect.
A brief downtick after the figures had soon reversed, as the market took its cue from bunds and treasuries. Bunds staged a late rally as short-covering drove treasuries higher.
Continued shorts in 2001 and 2002 guilder paper had fuelled activity in this segment, with 2001s continuing attractive against Germany, one dealer said.
"That's a trade that's been going on for three days now," she added, but noted volumes were low.
